# aembit_resource_set (Resource)

Resource to create and manage Resource Sets in an Aembit Cloud tenant.

~> **Default System Roles & Association Ownership**:
   - **System Roles**: Aembit automatically assigns the tenant's built-in `SuperAdmin` and `Auditor` roles to every Resource Set.
     - When `roles` is omitted or `null`, Terraform treats `roles` as computed, reflecting all backend-associated roles (including default system roles and any custom roles assigned via `aembit_role.resource_sets_assignments`).
     - When `roles` is explicitly configured (e.g., `roles = [aembit_role.example.id]` or `roles = []`), Terraform tracks only your configured custom roles in `roles`, while `effective_roles` always contains the full backend-assigned set (including `SuperAdmin` and `Auditor`).
   - **Single-Sided Ownership**: Manage Role-to-ResourceSet associations on either `aembit_resource_set.roles` or `aembit_role.resource_sets_assignments`, **never both**.
     - **Pattern A (Manage on `aembit_role`)**: Configure `resource_sets_assignments` on `aembit_role` and **omit** `roles` on `aembit_resource_set` (or use `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [roles] }`). **Do not set `roles = []`** on `aembit_resource_set` when managing associations from `aembit_role`, as `roles = []` instructs Terraform to enforce an empty custom role list and causes plan drift.
     - **Pattern B (Manage on `aembit_resource_set`)**: Configure `roles` on `aembit_resource_set`, set `resource_sets_assignments = []` on `aembit_role`, and configure `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [resource_sets_assignments] }` on `aembit_role` to prevent Terraform from applying the default Default Resource Set assignment.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# 1. Default system roles: roles omitted (system automatically assigns SuperAdmin and Auditor; both appear in effective_roles)
resource "aembit_resource_set" "default_roles" {
  name        = "Workloads - Default Roles"
  description = "Resource Set with default system role assignments"
}

# 2. Explicit empty custom roles: roles = [] (or module/variable fallback try(each.value.roles, []))
# SuperAdmin and Auditor are still assigned by the backend and exposed in effective_roles
resource "aembit_resource_set" "empty_custom_roles" {
  name        = "Workloads - Explicit Empty Custom Roles"
  description = "Resource Set configured with explicit empty custom roles"
  roles       = []
}

# 3. Custom role assignment: resource set configured with explicit custom roles
# Note: When managing associations from aembit_role (Pattern A), omit roles on aembit_resource_set instead
resource "aembit_resource_set" "custom_roles" {
  name        = "Workloads - Custom Roles"
  description = "Resource Set configured with custom role assignments"
  roles       = [aembit_role.example.id]
}

resource "aembit_role" "example" {
  name        = "Example Custom Role"
  description = "Role associated with custom resource set"
  is_active   = true

  access_policies                    = { read = true, write = false }
  client_workloads                   = { read = true, write = false }
  trust_providers                    = { read = true, write = false }
  access_conditions                  = { read = true, write = false }
  integrations                       = { read = true, write = false }
  credential_providers               = { read = true, write = false }
  credential_provider_integrations   = { read = true, write = false }
  server_workloads                   = { read = true, write = false }
  agent_controllers                  = { read = true, write = false }
  discovery_integrations             = { read = true, write = false }
  standalone_certificate_authorities = { read = true, write = false }

  access_authorization_events     = { read = true }
  global_policy_compliance_report = { read = true }
  audit_logs                      = { read = true }
  workload_events                 = { read = true }

  users                    = { read = true, write = false }
  roles                    = { read = true, write = false }
  log_streams              = { read = true, write = false }
  identity_providers       = { read = true, write = false }
  signon_policy            = { read = true, write = false }
  global_policy_compliance = { read = true, write = false }
  resource_sets            = { read = true, write = false }
  routing                  = { read = true, write = false }

  resource_sets_assignments = []
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [resource_sets_assignments]
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name for the ResourceSet.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description for the ResourceSet.
- `roles` (Set of String) IDs of the Roles associated with this Resource Set. Aembit automatically assigns the tenant's SuperAdmin and Auditor roles to every Resource Set. If omitted or null, Terraform treats this attribute as computed, reflecting all backend-associated roles (including default system roles and any custom roles assigned via aembit_role.resource_sets_assignments). If set to an explicit set of custom role IDs or an empty set ([]), Terraform tracks only the configured role IDs in this attribute while exposing the full backend-assigned set (including SuperAdmin and Auditor) in effective_roles. Manage Role-to-ResourceSet associations on either aembit_resource_set.roles or aembit_role.resource_sets_assignments, not both; if managing associations on aembit_role.resource_sets_assignments, omit roles on aembit_resource_set (or use lifecycle { ignore_changes = [roles] }) rather than setting roles = [].
- `standalone_certificate_authority` (String) Standalone Certificate Authority ID configured for this ResourceSet.

### Read-Only

- `effective_roles` (Set of String) Complete set of Role IDs in effect for this Resource Set, including system-assigned roles (SuperAdmin and Auditor) and any configured custom roles.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the ResourceSet.
